hunks.baseline: Hong Woojin was furious enough to burst. If he had entered the cat’s body like last time, he would have puffed up its fur and hissed.
hunks.sol: Hong Woojin was furious enough to burst. If he had entered the cat’s body like last time, he would have bristled its fur and hissed.

hunks.baseline: The target of his anger was the fly that kept entering the house.
hunks.sol: The target of his anger was the endless stream of flies entering the house.

hunks.baseline: Woojin did not know who was behind them, but whoever it was seemed to think they were being careful by sneaking the flies in one at a time. Instead, they were only putting Jin Taekyung further on guard.
hunks.sol: Woojin did not know who was behind them, but whoever it was seemed to think they were being careful by sneaking the flies in one at a time. Instead, they were only making Jin Taekyung more suspicious.

hunks.baseline: A predictable end. Hong Woojin grew anxious, worried that Jin Taekyung might notice him.
hunks.sol: The inevitable end. Hong Woojin grew anxious, worried that Jin Taekyung might notice him.

hunks.baseline: That fly was a Familiar being controlled by a mage. The proof was the incredibly faint mana that only another mage could sense.
hunks.sol: That fly was a Familiar being controlled by a mage. The proof was the incredibly faint trace of mana that only another mage could sense.

hunks.baseline: *Who hired the bastard? Sangdong Guild, after all?*
hunks.sol: *Who hired the bastard? Was it Sangdong Guild after all?*

hunks.baseline: If that was the case, he would have to quit this assignment right away. He was a professional with immense pride in his abilities.
hunks.sol: If that was the case, he would have to quit this assignment immediately. He was a professional with immense pride in his abilities.

hunks.baseline: *I told them over and over…*
hunks.sol: *I warned them over and over…*

hunks.baseline: Swallowing his curses, Hong Woojin hurriedly moved his body. He was wriggling deeper into a place no human eyes could reach when—
hunks.sol: Swallowing a curse, Hong Woojin wriggled deeper into a place no human eyes could reach. Then—

hunks.baseline: He was seized by a strange sensation, as if his body had suddenly floated into the air. It had never happened once since he began using Familiar magic.
hunks.sol: A strange sensation seized him, as though his body had suddenly floated into the air. It had never happened once since he began using Familiar magic.

hunks.baseline: The sensation lasted only an instant, but Hong Woojin could not shake off his unease. For a moment, he wondered whether it had been some kind of detection spell, but he soon shook his head.
hunks.sol: The sensation lasted only an instant, but Hong Woojin could not shake his unease. For a moment, he wondered whether it had been some kind of detection spell, but he soon shook his head.

hunks.baseline: The decisive reason he convinced himself it had been a simple illusion was Jin Taekyung’s reaction.
hunks.sol: What finally convinced him that he had imagined it was Jin Taekyung’s reaction.

hunks.baseline: “Maybe its wing’s injured. This fly’s looking pretty weak.”
hunks.sol: “Maybe its wing’s injured. This fly looks pretty weak.”

hunks.baseline: With a crisp sound, Jin Taekyung returned to the living room and sprawled out on the sofa. He chuckled at a variety show for a while, but soon the house was filled with loud snoring instead of laughter.
hunks.sol: With a crisp sound, Jin Taekyung returned to the living room and sprawled out on the sofa. He chuckled at a variety show for a while, but soon loud snoring replaced his laughter and filled the house.

hunks.baseline: Grrrrr. Grrrrr.
hunks.sol: Hrrrnk. Hrrrnk.

hunks.baseline: The incident from two days ago still lingered in the back of his mind. He had been watching Jin Taekyung through a cat Familiar and had been startled by what happened. For some reason, it had continued to bother him ever since. Now, at last, he felt he could breathe a little easier.
hunks.sol: The incident from two days ago still lingered in the back of his mind. He had been watching Jin Taekyung through a cat Familiar when the man suddenly startled him. For some reason, it had continued to bother him ever since. Now, at last, he felt he could breathe a little easier.

hunks.baseline: *If he can’t even recognize a shoddy Familiar like this, then that says it all.*
hunks.sol: *If he can’t even recognize a shoddy Familiar like that, then that says it all.*

hunks.baseline: Hong Woojin had chosen a rice weevil from among all the living creatures in the world because he had retained a sliver of caution toward Jin Taekyung.
hunks.sol: Hong Woojin had chosen a rice weevil from among all the living creatures in the world because he still harbored a sliver of caution toward Jin Taekyung.

hunks.baseline: Grrrrr…
hunks.sol: Hrrrnk…

hunks.baseline: A faint presence disappeared. I could sense the change only because I was using every one of my senses.
hunks.sol: A faint presence disappeared. I could sense the change only because I was focusing every one of my senses.

hunks.baseline: Only ten minutes ago, its Level window had carried the tag “Familiar.” Not anymore—not with the Link severed.
hunks.sol: Only ten minutes ago, its Level window had carried the tag “Familiar.” Not anymore, now that the Link had been severed.

hunks.baseline: I got up from the sofa and casually walked around the house. Only then could I be certain.
hunks.sol: I got up from the sofa and casually wandered around the house. Only then could I be certain.

hunks.baseline: The only things caught by my Qi Sense were a few ordinary flying insects. There was no Familiar anywhere.
hunks.sol: The only things caught by my Qi Sense were a few ordinary flying insects. There was not a Familiar among them.

hunks.baseline: The buzzing of wings that had continued without pause had stopped, too.
hunks.sol: The incessant buzzing of wings had stopped, too.

hunks.baseline: They had probably gotten spooked by what just happened, so at least they would not show their faces for the rest of the day.
hunks.sol: What had just happened had probably spooked them, so they would at least stay away for the rest of the day.

hunks.baseline: *Damn it. A Familiar?*
hunks.sol: *Damn it. Familiars?*

hunks.baseline: It was a kind of mental magic used by mages. The caster formed a mental connection with the creature chosen as a Familiar and, depending on the caster’s skill, could even control it at will.
hunks.sol: It was a type of mental magic used by mages. The caster formed a mental connection with the creature chosen as a Familiar and, depending on their skill, could even control it at will.

hunks.baseline: A melee Hunter was not automatically a master of every weapon, and mages were the same. Mental magic, in particular, was said to be among the more difficult branches.
hunks.sol: Just as melee Hunters were not automatically masters of every weapon, mages had their own specialties. Mental magic, in particular, was said to be one of the more difficult branches.

hunks.baseline: The only place I had formed some kind of grudge against in the real world was Sangdong Guild. More precisely, Im Changsoo.
hunks.sol: The only people I had any sort of grudge against in the real world were from Sangdong Guild. More precisely, Im Changsoo.

hunks.baseline: If what happened today was his order, this would not end easily.
hunks.sol: If what happened today had been his order, this would not end easily.

hunks.baseline: But I could not tolerate what happened today. This was my home, the place where my beloved family lived. They had touched my one inviolable boundary.
hunks.sol: But I could not tolerate what happened today. This was my home, the place where my beloved family lived. They had crossed my one inviolable boundary.

hunks.baseline: Her face was stiff. Had they used a Familiar to pull something behind my back? My thoughts grew frantic.
hunks.sol: Her face was stiff. Had they used a Familiar to pull something behind my back? My thoughts raced.

hunks.baseline: Right. I had been underestimating you far too much.
hunks.sol: Right. I had underestimated you by far too much.

hunks.baseline: My eyes felt gritty from staying alert all night in preparation for another Familiar’s intrusion with Qi Sense, but I shook off the fatigue by circulating my qi.
hunks.sol: My eyes felt gritty from staying alert with Qi Sense all night in case another Familiar intruded, but I shook off the fatigue by circulating my qi.

hunks.baseline: The taxi sped along the wide-open roads without a hitch, reaching the destination much faster than I had expected.
hunks.sol: The taxi sped along the empty roads without a hitch, reaching the destination much faster than I had expected.

hunks.baseline: *Is this my first time coming to the Store since I visited once a few years ago?*
hunks.sol: *Is this my first time coming to the Store since I visited a few years ago?*

hunks.baseline: The Store, located in the center of Ilsan, stood out clearly even from a distance. For one thing, it was overwhelmingly larger and more splendid than the shops around it.
hunks.sol: Located in the center of Ilsan, the Store stood out even from a distance. For one thing, it was overwhelmingly larger and more lavish than the shops around it.

hunks.baseline: There was another thing that set it apart from ordinary stores. At the entrance, guards in suits were screening the customers.
hunks.sol: There was another thing that set it apart. Guards in suits were screening customers at the entrance.

hunks.baseline: “Because the fingerprint scanner says you’re not adults.”
hunks.sol: “Because the fingerprint scanner says you aren’t.”

hunks.baseline: “Isn’t it defective?”
hunks.sol: “Isn’t it broken?”

hunks.baseline: Five or six teenagers who looked obviously young flinched and took a step back.
hunks.sol: The five or six teenagers, all of whom looked obviously underage, flinched and took a step back.

hunks.baseline: “Customers to me are Hunters or civilian adults who’ve been issued membership cards. Not high school punks like you.”
hunks.sol: “My customers are Hunters and civilian adults with membership cards. Not high school punks like you.”

hunks.baseline: People like that existed everywhere. Especially in a Store filled with all kinds of goods ordinary people could never access.
hunks.sol: There were people like that everywhere, but the Store—filled with all kinds of goods ordinary people could never access—attracted even more of them.

hunks.baseline: Only after the kids loitering in front had left did the guard notice me. He addressed me politely.
hunks.sol: Only after the kids loitering out front had left did the guard notice me. He addressed me politely.

hunks.baseline: “I’ll need to complete the verification process.”
hunks.sol: “I’ll need to verify it.”

hunks.baseline: The items stocked on each floor of the Store were different. I had visited once when I was an F-rank Hunter, but the second floor had been the highest I could access at the time. I had never even gotten to look around above it.
hunks.sol: The Store stocked different items on each floor. I had visited once when I was an F-rank Hunter, but the second floor had been the highest I could access at the time. I had never even gotten to look around above it.

hunks.baseline: “Have a pleasant time.”
hunks.sol: “Have a pleasant visit.”

hunks.baseline: “Thank you. Have a good one.”
hunks.sol: “Thanks. Take care.”

hunks.sol: The space was incomparably larger than an ordinary shop, yet there were only a handful of customers in sight.

hunks.sol: Only a tiny minority could shop here: Hunters, who made up just 0.1 percent of Korea’s population, and civilians with enough social influence to be issued membership cards.

hunks.sol: Employees were busy explaining products to their customers.

hunks.sol: That was right. The Store was essentially a luxury department store where people could buy expensive magical goods that were difficult to obtain through ordinary channels.

hunks.sol: “Don’t you have anything better? Don’t worry about the price. Bring me some options.”

hunks.sol: Now that I was a C-rank Hunter, the customer service was considerably more attentive.

hunks.sol: Assistant Manager Kim Seonhee secretly sighed at the customer’s words. As someone unusually concerned about her sales numbers, this was far from welcome news.

hunks.sol: A colleague who had joined the company at the same time as her and worked at the Seoul branch was already a Team Leader. Whether it was luck or business savvy, apparently every customer she encountered was a big spender.

hunks.sol: “It’s currently part of our summer promotion, so we’re offering it at the low price of 520,000 won.”

hunks.sol: How much did a C-rank Hunter make a year again? Didn’t their basic allowances alone amount to several hundred million won? Kim Seonhee found it ridiculous, but silently waited for the customer to make his choice.
